notes: One row per health indicator. Drives body map colours, Learn cards, reminders, alert thresholds and agent retrieval. 'personal' rules compare with the astronaut's own baseline; 'absolute' rules use fixed clinical or NASA limits. Clinical cut-offs marked 'general clinical reference' should be confirmed with a medical mentor before any real use.

indicators.name: Blood pressure
indicators.risk: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
indicators.space_effect: Fluid shifts toward the head and blood volume falls; pressure patterns change in flight and many crew struggle to keep pressure up when standing after landing.
indicators.why_measure: Shows how the heart and vessels are adapting, and is the baseline for landing-day readiness.
actions: Re-measure after 5 min rest, arm at heart level
Report headache or vision change with it

indicators.name: Resting heart rate and rhythm
indicators.risk: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
indicators.space_effect: The heart works less without gravity and can lose fitness; rhythm problems are rare but would be serious far from Earth.
indicators.why_measure: Catches rhythm problems early and tracks fitness loss.
actions: If irregular with dizziness or chest symptoms: emergency, start Triage

indicators.name: Heart-rate variability (RMSSD)
indicators.risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
indicators.space_effect: Falls with stress, poor sleep and illness.
indicators.why_measure: An early, objective stress and recovery signal.

indicators.name: Blood oxygen
indicators.risk: Risk of Hypoxia
indicators.space_effect: Cabin oxygen is engineered; a drop can mean an atmosphere or lung problem.
indicators.why_measure: Simple early warning for both the person and the cabin air.
actions: Check cabin O2 and CO2 readings

indicators.name: Body temperature
indicators.risk: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses
indicators.space_effect: The immune system is weakened in flight, so infections and reactivated viruses are more likely.
indicators.why_measure: Fever is the simplest sign of infection.

indicators.name: Blood sugar (fasting)
indicators.risk: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
indicators.space_effect: Stress hormones and lower activity can push blood sugar up.
indicators.why_measure: Named by the challenge brief; tracks metabolic health.
actions: If under 70: fast sugar now and re-test in 15 min

indicators.name: Sleep duration
indicators.risk: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
indicators.space_effect: Astronauts averaged about 6 h of sleep on ISS despite 8.5 h scheduled; sleep loss reduces alertness and performance.
indicators.why_measure: Short sleep builds up into slower reactions and mistakes.

indicators.name: Mood (self-report 1-5)
indicators.risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
indicators.space_effect: Isolation, confinement and workload can lower mood over long missions.
indicators.why_measure: Named by the challenge brief; behavioural changes are easier to address early.
actions: Schedule a private call with the behavioural health team

indicators.name: Face fatigue (PERCLOS)
indicators.risk: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
indicators.space_effect: Fatigue shows in eye closure and blinking before people notice it.
indicators.why_measure: Objective fatigue signal to pair with sleep data.
actions: Avoid critical tasks in the next 2 h

indicators.name: Vision check (Amsler grid + near acuity)
indicators.risk: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
indicators.space_effect: Fluid shift can change the eye and optic nerve; most long-duration astronauts show at least one SANS sign.
indicators.why_measure: NASA's leading spaceflight health risk; early changes are worth reporting even without symptoms.

indicators.name: Bone index (exercise load + urine calcium)
indicators.risk: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
indicators.space_effect: Weight-bearing bones lose on average 1-1.5% of density per month on 4-6 month missions.
indicators.why_measure: Loss is silent; only trends show it. Exercise is the main countermeasure.

indicators.name: Fluid intake
indicators.risk: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
indicators.space_effect: Thirst is blunted in flight; low fluid raises kidney stone risk alongside bone calcium loss.
indicators.why_measure: Easy to fix, easy to forget.

indicators.name: Calcium intake
indicators.risk: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
indicators.space_effect: Bone loss releases calcium; intake must stay in range to support bone.
indicators.why_measure: Supports the bone countermeasure.
actions: Add a dairy or fortified pouch

indicators.name: Cabin CO2
indicators.risk: Risk of Hypoxia
indicators.space_effect: CO2 builds up in closed cabins; headaches are linked to levels between 2.8 and 4.5 mmHg.
indicators.why_measure: Explains headaches and poor focus that look like illness.
actions: Report to crew for scrubber check

indicators.name: Radiation dose rate
indicators.risk: Risk of Radiation-Induced Cancers
indicators.space_effect: Galactic cosmic rays give a steady dose; solar particle events can add a large dose quickly.
indicators.why_measure: Solar storms need fast sheltering.
actions: Move to storm shelter on red

indicators.name: Cumulative radiation dose
indicators.risk: Risk of Radiation-Induced Cancers
indicators.space_effect: NASA's career limit is 600 mSv effective dose; solar particle events are limited to 250 mSv per event.
indicators.why_measure: Mission planning and long-term cancer risk.
actions: Flight surgeon review of remaining exposure

indicators.name: Skin and lip check (photo + symptoms)
indicators.risk: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses
indicators.space_effect: Latent herpes viruses reactivate in over half of astronauts; rashes and cold sores are more common.
indicators.why_measure: Early sign of immune stress or infection.
actions: Photo log for the medical officer

indicators.name: Stand-up test (landing readiness)
indicators.risk: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
indicators.space_effect: After long flights many astronauts feel faint on standing; compression garments and fluid loading help.
indicators.why_measure: Decides how much help someone needs after landing.

indicators.name: Reaction time (alertness test)
indicators.risk: Risk of Performance Decrements from Sleep Loss and Work Overload
indicators.space_effect: Short sleep, shifted schedules and high workload slow reactions before people feel tired.
indicators.why_measure: A slow morning score is an early sign to rest before critical tasks.
actions: Avoid critical tasks for 2 h and take a short rest

indicators.name: Exercise done
indicators.risk: Risk of Reduced Muscle Mass, Strength and Endurance
indicators.space_effect: Without gravity, muscles and bones weaken quickly; ISS crews exercise about 2 hours a day to slow this.
indicators.why_measure: Exercise is the main countermeasure; missed days add up.
actions: Split exercise into two shorter blocks

indicators.name: Body mass
indicators.risk: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
indicators.space_effect: Many astronauts eat less in space and lose body mass, which speeds muscle and bone loss.
indicators.why_measure: A steady fall means not enough food or muscle loss.
actions: Add one extra meal pouch per day
Review the food log with the crew medical officer

indicators.name: Back pain
indicators.risk: Risk of Reduced Muscle Mass, Strength and Endurance
indicators.space_effect: The spine lengthens in weightlessness and back pain is common, mostly early in flight.
indicators.why_measure: Pain that stays or grows needs the crew medical officer.
actions: Tell the crew medical officer if it lasts 3 days
